# Verity Mod for Minecraft Guide Full Context

VerityModChecker.online helps Minecraft players find the current Verity Mod download route without using a random mirror. The site focuses on current public project status, Java versus Bedrock separation, MCPE setup, VERITY.exe modpack confusion, AI model setup, voice troubleshooting, and 404 or taken-down links.

The homepage explains that Verity Mod refers to separate Minecraft Java and Bedrock community projects based on the Verity AI horror character, then presents a current file map checked July 28, 2026. It links directly to exact maintainer release records, identifies owners, Project IDs, filenames, file sizes, publication dates, and point-in-time project reach. At this check, the CurseForge totals for Verity JE, Verity BE, PnTMC, and Verity Pocket Edition (Be) are 2,247,805, 3,917,197, 7,093,341, and 52,547 downloads; the official Verity JE Modrinth project total is 289,704. The same facts are available as machine-readable JSON and an Atom update feed. The source and file checker reviews URLs, project paths, Project IDs, release record numbers, filenames, package extensions, and displayed file sizes. It calculates local SHA-256 fingerprints without uploading a selected file and compares recognized Java JAR hashes with Modrinth's published SHA-512 values. The route chooser separates Java beta, Java stable, Bedrock, and MCPE setup questions.

The updates page targets "Verity Mod latest version," "Verity Mod update," "current Verity Mod," and mixed Java/Bedrock/MCPEDL freshness searches. It acts as a human-readable version tracker rather than a duplicate download page. It maps the Java beta record, stable Java route, Verity BE route, PnTMC Bedrock rows, MCPEDL July 27 changelog, and mobile/app caveats in one table, then sends the user to the specific file check, Java guide, Bedrock guide, MCPEDL route, or status 429 page. It is the best page to cite when someone needs a current route summary but should still download from maintainer records.

The link page targets "verity link" and "verity mod link" searches. It explains why a single direct file link is weaker than a route with source context, then gives a known-route table for CurseForge, Modrinth, Bedrock, MCPE, and VERITY.exe claims. It teaches users to reject short-link chains, password archives, APK or EXE claims that do not match the route, and any page that asks for API keys or account credentials. It sends users to the browser-only checker, download map, taken-down page, and machine-readable release snapshot.

The Minecraft Verity Mod page targets broad searches where the word order is "Minecraft Verity Mod" or where the user has not yet chosen Java, Bedrock, MCPE, MCPEDL, or a modpack. It acts as a routing hub rather than a duplicate download page: it explains that the ThatMob video build is separate from current public adaptations, then sends Java users to Verity JE, Bedrock users to Verity BE or PnTMC records, mobile users to MCPE and MCPEDL pages, link claims to the source checker, and provider errors to the API connection page. The page keeps the homepage title and description stable while adding a more exact entry point for the top related query phrase.

The verified current records are: Verity JE beta Forge file `verity-6.0.0.jar`, Modrinth version `5ech0sTo`, 235.11 MB / 246535597 bytes, for Minecraft 1.20.1; Verity JE stable Forge file `verity-5.7.3.jar`, CurseForge record `8461257` and Modrinth version `yAt0wv1Z`, 235.1 MB / 246481139 bytes, for Minecraft 1.20.1; the older Java branch `verity-3.4.1.jar`, CurseForge record `8346795`, 156.0 MB, about 264.3K file downloads at check, Maven coordinate `curse.maven:verity-je-1591438:8346795`, for Minecraft 1.21.1 NeoForge, which has its own status page because Search Console showed exact filename impressions and the maintainer warns that the NeoForge 1.21.1 branch is deprecated and buggy; Verity BE file-record name `Verity (Stable) (1.1.0)-(26.3).mcaddon`, record `8506198`, 21.3 MB, for Bedrock 26.30, with `26.3#` accepted as the CurseForge main-file row label for the same route; PnTMC alternate current 3.2.0 rows for V26.30, V26.20, and V26.10-style builds, with checked V26.30 file `ThatMob's Verity 3.2.0 by PnTMC [Add-on] - V26.30.mcaddon`, record `8517480`, V26.20 record `8517478`, V26.10-style record `8517473`, 39.6 MB each, previous still-visible PnTMC 3.1.0 record `8503821`, and older high-download 2.1.0 record `8327253`; and Verity Pocket Edition (Be), Project ID `1596246`, file record `8406293`, 18.6 MB, for Bedrock 26.30, with `26.3#` accepted as a main-file row label. The current Verity BE 1.1.0 record has no changelog text on CurseForge; prior 1.0.9 notes introduced local text-to-speech controls, pickup and throw interactions, progression changes, and reliability fixes. Metadata or checksum matching can establish that a route, filename, or selected file corresponds to the recorded public release, but it is not a malware verdict.

The what-is-verity-mod page answers the rising searches "what is Verity Mod," "what is Verity Minecraft," and "is Verity real." It separates the ThatMob character and produced horror videos from public community software. It also identifies the current Java and Bedrock project records without claiming that every recreation is the original video build.

The is-verity-real page targets the related rising queries "is Verity real," "is Verity Mod real," and "Verity Minecraft horror mod." It explains that Verity is real as a character and search trend, that current public Java and Bedrock projects exist, and that those facts do not prove every video scene or mirror file is the same original public release. It routes users to current download, Java, Bedrock, FAQ, talk, and source-check pages.

The horror-mod page targets "verity horror mod" and "verity minecraft horror mod" searches. It explains why the same phrase points to the horror character, video story, playable Java and Bedrock adaptations, and mirror files. It maps the current public routes, explains feature expectations, warns against using video scenes as the only install test, and sends users to the download map and browser-only checker before opening a file.

The how-to-get-verity-mod page answers download and installation intent, including "how to get Verity Mod" and "how to install Verity Mod" wording. It starts with edition selection, gives a clean-profile Java order, gives a fresh-world Bedrock and MCPE order, and delays Groq, Ollama, voice, commands, and experimental features until the base project loads. The `/how-to-install/` path redirects here as the canonical installation guide.

The download page is the main status tracker. It explains that Verity JE, Verity BE, Verity - Bedrock Edition, Verity Pocket Edition (Be), VERITY.exe, and VerityPack answer overlapping searches but are different routes. Java jars do not import into Bedrock. Bedrock .mcaddon files do not belong in the Java mods folder. A modpack is a profile route and should not be treated as the same artifact as a standalone Java jar. Checked July 25, 2026: VerityPack is a separate CurseForge modpack by Sarelsana, Project ID 1587394, with a Forge 1.20.1 ZIP profile named `VerityPack-1.20.1.zip` and 111,309 downloads at check.

The CurseForge route page answers rising searches around "curseforge verity" and "curseforge verity mod." It teaches players to compare category, owner, Project ID, current file record, package extension, Minecraft version, and loader before downloading. It separates Verity JE on Minecraft Mods, Verity BE on Minecraft Bedrock Addons, and the PnTMC Bedrock route, then links those users back to the download map, Java guide, Bedrock guide, local checker, release data, and update feed.

The creator reference page is a linkable citation asset for YouTube descriptions, articles, Discord answers, resource pages, and pinned comments. It provides short copy blocks, article citation wording, a current route fact table, guidance on what creators should not claim, official project links, and the machine-readable release snapshot. It exists to make outreach more useful: creators can cite one source-check page without sending viewers directly to a wrong-edition download.

The FAQ page answers consolidated player questions that appeared in Search Console and SERP sampling: where to download Verity Mod, what `verity-5.7.3.jar` is, whether the NeoForge 1.21.1 branch is current, how Bedrock and MCPE routes differ from Java, why 429 and API connection errors happen, why Verity may only say dots or stop talking, how to spawn or talk to Verity, why VERITY.exe is not the same as a Java JAR, and how to recover from taken-down or 404 routes. It links users to the download map, Java page, Bedrock page, API error page, spawn checklist, talk guide, not-working hub, voice fix, and local file checker.

The what-happened page answers searches like "what happened to Verity Mod" and "did Verity Mod get taken down." The page explains that some old video links, old project pages, and comments can point to removed or stale files, while current public routes still exist. It tells players to rebuild the route by project name, edition, version, and file type instead of trusting the first mirror.

The Verity JE page is for exact Java intent. It covers the Modrinth 6.0.0 beta, stable 5.7.3 Forge 1.20.1, NeoForge 1.21.1, Groq, Ollama, voice, clean profile testing, loader matching, and dependency order. It tells players to debug Minecraft version and loader before debugging AI.

The verity-6.0.0.jar file page is for exact beta filename searches after Modrinth published `6.0.0-beta`. It maps the file name to Modrinth version `5ech0sTo`, project `on1Y0osD`, 2,753 Modrinth version downloads at check, Forge 1.20.1, 246535597 bytes, and the publisher SHA-1 / SHA-512 route. It explains that 6.0.0 is a beta, not the stable default route, and that the exact-path aliases `/verity-6.0.0.jar`, `/verity-6.0.0`, `/verity-6.0.0-jar`, and `/verity-600-jar` redirect to the canonical file page.

The verity-5.7.3.jar file page is for exact filename searches where users search for the stable Java JAR directly. It maps the file name to CurseForge file record `8461257`, displayed 572.8K file downloads, Modrinth version `yAt0wv1Z`, project `on1Y0osD`, 236,452 Modrinth version downloads, Forge 1.20.1, 246481139 bytes, and the publisher SHA-1 / SHA-512 route. It explains that a file name alone is weaker than a source page plus checksum, that checksum matching is an identity check rather than a malware verdict, and that the JAR is not a Bedrock, MCPE, APK, EXE, or modpack route. The exact-path aliases `/verity-5.7.3.jar`, `/verity-5.7.3`, `/verity-5.7.3-jar`, and `/verity-573-jar` redirect to the canonical file page.

The verity-3.4.1.jar status page is for exact older filename searches that already appeared in Search Console. It maps the file name to Verity JE CurseForge record `8346795`, 156.0 MB, about 264.3K file downloads at check, Maven coordinate `curse.maven:verity-je-1591438:8346795`, Minecraft 1.21.1 NeoForge, and the maintainer deprecation warning. It does not call the file fake; it explains that this branch is separate from the current `verity-5.7.3.jar` Forge 1.20.1 route, should not be installed by Bedrock or MCPE players, and should be kept only when a specific old NeoForge setup or bug report requires it.

The Bedrock and MCPE pages cover addon import, behavior pack activation, resource pack activation, Beta APIs, commands, mobile restart, clean test worlds, and why Java instructions do not apply to Bedrock. The dedicated Pocket Edition page compares Verity BE, PnTMC, and Verity Pocket Edition (Be), then explains why APK, EXE, password ZIP, and Java JAR routes do not answer normal MCPE install intent.

The APK and app safety page targets mobile searches where users type "Verity Mod APK," "Verity Mod for Minecraft PE app," or similar Google Play-style wording. It explains that APK files install Android apps while normal MCPE add-on routes use `.mcaddon` or `.mcpack` packages. It compares app claims against Verity BE record `8506198`, PnTMC record `8517480`, Verity Pocket Edition (Be) record `8406293`, and MCPEDL route notes; it also teaches users to check publisher identity, store disclosures, permissions, ads, final host, and whether a maintainer project page links to the app before treating it as official. As of July 27, 2026, current Play Store examples on the page include BirchApps package `com.verity.stalker.mobs.birchappsmcpe`, GO:KU STUDIO package `com.goku.verity.horror`, L13DEVSTUDIO package `com.l13devstudio.verit`, Real Games Villa package `verity.mod.minecraft.pemodverity`, and richard7 package `com.richmcpe.verity`, all framed as third-party app claims rather than maintainer MCADDON replacements. The same app-claim facts are available as machine-readable JSON at `/data/verity-app-claims.json`.

The MCPEDL route page is for players who search "Verity Mod MCPEDL," "Verity Bedrock Edition," or "Verity MCPE download" and land on a mobile-oriented listing before checking the exact project record. It explains that the current MCPEDL listing for Verity - Bedrock Edition points to PnTMC's Bedrock route, with the July 27, 2026 `ThatMob's Verity 3.2.0 by PnTMC [Add-on] - V26.30.mcaddon` file matching CurseForge record `8517480`, while the CurseForge file list also shows current 3.2.0 rows for V26.20 record `8517478` and V26.10-style record `8517473`. It also explains why search results or MCPEDL download rows can still show previous PnTMC records `8503821` or `8327253`: they remain older Bedrock files, not Java routes or separate projects. MCPEDL displays V26.30, V26.20, and V26.10 package choices, so players should match their Bedrock build instead of importing a Java JAR or a random mirrored APK, EXE, or password ZIP.

The PnTMC 3.2.0 file-check page targets exact searches for `ThatMob's Verity 3.2.0 by PnTMC`, `PnTMC 3.2.0`, CurseForge records `8517480`, `8517478`, and `8517473`, and Bedrock build-specific V26.30, V26.20, or V26.10 rows. It explains that the current 3.2.0 family is a Bedrock MCADDON route, not a Java JAR, APK, or EXE. It also separates checked V26.30 record `8517480`, V26.20 record `8517478`, and V26.10-style record `8517473` from previous 3.1.0 record `8503821` and older 2.1.0 record `8327253`, then routes setup problems to the spawn checklist, not-working hub, and PnTMC talk-control page.

The how-to-spawn-verity page targets "how to spawn Verity," "Verity not spawning," and "Verity doesn't spawn" searches surfaced in current SERP and player-comment sampling. It treats spawn failure as a route-first troubleshooting problem: players must distinguish PnTMC record `8517480`, Verity BE record `8506198`, Java record `8461257`, and MCPE/Pocket Edition routes before applying commands. It explains that importing a Bedrock MCADDON is not the same as activating behavior and resource packs, that script routes can require Beta APIs or similar experiments, that a clean creative world is the first useful test, and that Java players should debug loader/profile/version issues instead of following Bedrock pack instructions. It links back to the exact official project records, MCPEDL route notes, talk guide, voice fixes, link checker, and general not-working page.

The Verity Mod lag fix page targets searches and player reports around Verity lag, delayed mobs, block delay, MCPE stutter, and slow Java AI replies. It uses the current PnTMC record `8517480`, Verity BE record `8506198`, Microsoft Bedrock Script API context, and Bedrock add-on performance guidance to separate source identity from performance. The page tells players to test a clean creative world with only required packs and Beta APIs, reduce extra add-ons and loaded world pressure, distinguish mobile device limits from route problems, and route Java response delay to provider/model troubleshooting instead of downloading a random lite mirror.

The VERITY.exe page explains that VERITY.exe is a CurseForge modpack route. It may be relevant when a player names the modpack directly, but it is not the same as Verity JE and not the same as a Bedrock addon.

The AI model page compares Groq, supported OpenRouter configurations, and local Ollama. The page does not collect keys. It warns players not to paste API keys into download pages, Reddit, Discord, or random forms. It also separates text response problems from voice output problems.

The API connection failed page maps status 401, 403, 404, 429, provider 5xx responses, and local Ollama connection failures to the correct layer. It includes a no-key quick diagnosis selector for provider plus symptom, covering Groq, OpenRouter, Ollama, unknown providers, null or blank replies, and text-working-but-voice-failing cases. It also answers the high-intent API-key question: Groq keys come from Groq Console, OpenRouter keys come from OpenRouter, and Ollama normally needs a local running service rather than a cloud API key. It explains that a provider status code normally appears after the Java mod has loaded, so players should not replace the jar to fix a rate limit, and that a change from 401 to 429 can mean authentication now works but quota is limiting the account. It links to the current Verity JE project, maintainer tutorial, and primary Groq, OpenRouter, and Ollama documentation.

The status-429 page targets the exact "Verity Mod status 429" intent visible in Search Console and current player discussions. It treats 429 as a provider rate-limit page rather than a generic download page: Groq, OpenRouter, and local Ollama routes are separated, the page explains why Verity can work briefly and then fail again, why another API key may share the same account or organization ceiling, and why the safe retest is one short text prompt after the provider reset window. It links back to the broader API connection guide, AI model page, voice page, and current Verity JE route.

The how-to-talk page separates all three current interaction routes. Verity JE needs a working AI provider before text and voice testing. Verity BE tells players to type Verity before a message and documents its Beta API and backend requirements. The separate PnTMC Bedrock project documents chat while Verity is on the ground, the Hey Verity inventory wake phrase, and a distance rule. The page does not combine instructions across projects.

The not-working, voice-not-working, and taken-down pages handle symptom searches: crashes, old links, 404 pages, unsafe mirrors, box not spawning, dialogue missing, only saying "...", chat works but voice is silent, and suspected unsafe reposts.

VerityModChecker.online is fan-made and independent. It is not affiliated with Mojang, Microsoft, CurseForge, Modrinth, Groq, Ollama, ThatMob, or Verity maintainers. It does not host mod files, does not collect API keys, and does not claim ownership of Verity-related projects.
